headlines.title: Chevron to Restart Ralston Biodiesel Facility in Iowa, Supported by Landus Cooperative Feedstock Supply Agreement
headlines.summary: HOUSTON & DES MOINES, Iowa, November 12, 2026--Chevron U.S.A. Inc., a subsidiary of Chevron Corporation (NYSE: CVX), announced today it will resume operation at its biodiesel production facility in Ralston, Iowa. The restart is supported by a commercial and operational agreement between Chevron and farmer-owned Landus Cooperative, an Iowa-based agriculture services cooperative.

headlines.title: What iShares Global Energy ETF (IXC) Sold: Exxon Mobil Leads on Nov. 10
headlines.summary: The fund sold $130.9 million of stock, cutting 26 positions and adding none, with Exxon Mobil and Chevron the largest reductions.

headlines.title: Exxon, Chevron, and Shell Just Reported. Here's What Each One Said About Where Oil Goes Next.
headlines.summary: Uncertainty is the main issue in the oil market, but that doesn't mean that these integrated energy giants aren't making plans.

headlines.title: How Chevron Is Maintaining Prominence in the Permian Basin
headlines.summary: With nearly 2 million acres and an interest in one out of every five wells in the Permian Basin, Chevron has recently reached a production plateau and turned its focus to increasing reliability and efficiency in its West Texas operations. On Bloomberg Chief Future Officer, CFO Eimear Bonner shows Annmarie Hordern some of the facilities and technologies that contribute to the company's competitive advantage in the region.

headlines.title: Patience Is Paying Off for Chevron in Venezuela
headlines.summary: Chevron has been operating in Venezuela since 1923, and remained in the country while many US energy companies left. CFO Eimear Bonner and CEO Mike Wirth discuss the new terms of Chevron's joint venture that's projected to double production in Venezuela over the next five years. They speak to Annmarie Hordern on "Chief Future Officer.

description: Chevron Corporation, through its subsidiaries, engages in the integrated energy and chemicals operations. It operates through Upstream and Downstream segments. The Upstream segment engages in the exploration for, development, production, and transportation of crude oil and natural gas; processing, liquefaction, transportation, and regasification of liquefied natural gas; transportation of crude oil through pipelines; transportation, storage, and marketing of natural gas; carbon capture and storage; and operation of a gas-to-liquids plant. The Downstream segment refines crude oil into petroleum products; markets crude oil, refined products, and lubricants; manufactures and markets renewable fuels; transports crude oil and refined products through pipeline, marine vessel, motor equipment, and rail car; and manufactures and markets commodity petrochemicals, plastics for industrial uses, and fuel and lubricant additives. The company operates in North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia. The company was formerly known as ChevronTexaco Corporation and changed its name to Chevron Corporation in May 2005. Chevron Corporation was founded in 1879 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.
